title: A 2.0.0 CLI refuses a workspace this release applied a generated set to, until `ia host claude --remove --apply` is run with this release
summary: The projection ownership state keeps its format name, ia.host-projection-state.v1, and now lists the generated agent and skill files beside the packet's, and .claude/settings.local.json holds one IA hook group per authored `@hook`, owned through .ia/distributions/hosts/claude-hooks-<id>.json. A published 2.0.0 @inventarch/cli or @inventarch/distribution on such a workspace: every `ia host claude` plan, apply or removal, `ia project claude` and the install refresh first look for IA guard groups, recognize each hook group by its launcher's guard arguments, find no 2.0.0 guard ownership state for it, and refuse with IA-DIST-LOCAL-MODIFICATION ("An IA guard group has no matching ownership state; remove only that guard group before retiring steward files"), which asks the user to delete IA's own group by hand; a state that lists a generated skill (.claude/skills/<name>/SKILL.md or .agents/skills/<name>/SKILL.md) is refused as an invalid projection ownership state (IA-DIST-INPUT-INVALID), for codex too; a claude state that lists generated agents and no skill reads each agent as a 1.x steward file and deletes it as legacy. Interrupted applies are refused too: while a hook registration is interrupted, guard-pending.json holds format ia.hook-registration-pending.v1, so 2.0.0 refuses host writes with IA-DIST-RECOVERY-REQUIRED and its `ia recover guard` refuses the journal as an unknown guard recovery format; and an interrupted projection apply leaves pending receipt evidence (<host>-receipt-pending.json) that may list a generated file's removal or carry removedHooks, which 2.0.0 refuses as invalid evidence, even for its own `--remove`. This release finishes both: `ia recover guard` for the journal, and its next `ia host <host> --apply` for the evidence. Trade-off (review finding H-N9): the state format name is kept rather than bumped. A new name only when generated paths are listed would turn 2.0.0's silent deletion of generated agents into a refusal, but it would also make 2.0.0 refuse every workspace this release applied a generated set to, and the hook groups, which that state does not hold, refuse in 2.0.0 either way. The deletion is accepted because a generated agent is regenerated from its record by this release's next apply. To hand a workspace back to a 2.0.0 CLI: if .ia/distributions/hosts/guard-pending.json exists, first run this release's `ia recover guard`, and if a <host>-receipt-pending.json exists, this release's `ia host <host> --apply`; then run `ia host claude --remove --apply` with this release (and `ia host codex --remove --apply` where codex is registered), which removes the hook groups, their ownership state, the generated files and the receipt, needing neither an admitting workspace nor readable records; then run 2.0.0's `ia host <claude|codex> --apply`. A workspace that authors no `@agent-profile`, `@playbook` or `@hook` gets no generated file or hook group written, so its projection and hook state stay as 2.0.0 reads them; its receipt only gains optional sections, which 2.0.0's reader ignores.
